## About

Vektorgeist is a research and development company working at the intersection
of AI, relational systems, and local-first technology.

Its research programme explores relational ontology, machine self-models, and
local-first AI: how things hold together, what a thing is, how its parts
relate, and what changes when those relations change.

That research is translated into experimental systems and practical tools:
local-first AI tools and other open-sourced instruments for observing and
changing relations inside working neural networks.

Vektorgeist was founded by Alexander Parnell and Lee Kersh. Alexander Parnell
is an independent researcher who publishes open-access research with permanent
DOIs through Zenodo.

## Research papers

All eleven papers are open access under CC-BY-4.0 with permanent DOIs on Zenodo.

1. The Hodos Hypothesis — What makes a thing the thing it is?
   DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21912354 (2026-09-04)
2. The Vektorgeist Method (VGM): How We Build Things —
   How do you build AI a person can own, inspect and trust?
   DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21613155 (2026-10-02)
3. The Afferent Gnosis Model: Self-Knowledge Without Self-Control —
   Can a machine's account of itself ever be trusted?
   DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21613153 (2026-09-04)
4. Hodos Diastema: Comparing Processes as Curves of Distributions —
   How do you compare two processes without throwing away time?
   DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21612829 (2026-09-04)
5. Learning Without Weights — What can a learner do with no trained
   parameters at all?
   DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21612831 (2026-09-04)
6. Beyond Weights: a Fixed Transmission Architecture for Learning Through
   Signal and Memory — What happens if you separate computation from knowledge?
   DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21850560 (2026-09-04)
7. The Hodos Family: Equations Generated by a Relational Premise —
   Does the premise generate anything beyond a ruler?
   DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21850666 (2026-09-04)
8. A Clock Made of Relations: Intrinsic duration for a system of interacting
   parts, read from its own relations — and the one-sided nonlinearity that hid
   it for thirteen attempts — Can the duration a process has lived be
   computed from its own internal relations?
   DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21861429 (2026-10-01)
9. A Control Blind by Construction: Testing a Conditional Claim About
   Trajectories — Two systems sit equally far from normal; one drifted over
   months, the other broke in seconds. Can the shape of the trajectory tell
   them apart?
   DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21850664 (2026-09-04)
10. The Law of Two: Why a Relational Ontology Entails Exactly Two —
    If nothing is what it is in isolation, how many things does it take to be
    one thing?
    DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21879204 (2026-09-04)
11. Relational Intelligence, Measured with Panaesthesis —
    Can you watch a working neural network's relations from the inside,
    change one, and measure what happens, reversibly?
    DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23088597 (2026-10-02)
    Open-source tool: https://github.com/xfloukiex-lab/panaesthesis
    (Apache-2.0; pip install panaesthesis)

## Panaesthesis

Vektorgeist's open-source instrument for observing and changing relations
inside working neural networks. One software, three instruments: the
Hodoscope watches every relation inside the model, live; the Hodotome changes
those relations; the Hodophylax stands guard over them.
- Install: pip install panaesthesis
- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/panaesthesis/
- GitHub: https://github.com/xfloukiex-lab/panaesthesis (Apache-2.0)
- Screenshots (desktop app, Hodos portrait render, animated splice demo):
  https://vektorgeist.github.io/floukie/#panaesthesis
